extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing creative writers (novice to intermediate)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, craft-focused advice for producing and revising fiction and memoir: how to start drafts, develop character and plot, write dialogue and detail, and manage the writer's inner life. Emphasizes small-step processes and intuitive work habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shitty First Drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only way I can get anything written at all is to write really, really shitty first drafts." Perfectionism is the enemy of creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get words on the page without self-censoring; accept an imperfect first draft as the necessary raw material to be refined in later revisions. Anti-pattern: delaying writing because you demand perfection from the first pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bird by Bird (work in small steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take overwhelming projects one small piece at a time — "Bird by bird, buddy. Just take it bird by bird."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break large projects into manageable, concrete tasks or scenes to avoid paralysis; focus on incremental progress rather than the entire scope at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 1-Inch Picture Frame (focus on a single scene)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at writing through a small frame — focus on a tiny scene, a single moment, rather than the entire daunting story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a narrow, highly focused scene to make progress, develop voice, and avoid getting overwhelmed by plot or structure decisions that can come later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polaroids (discover through writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of writing is like a Polaroid developing — you don't know what it'll look like until you write it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the work to reveal itself in the act of writing; embrace surprises and discoveries rather than trying to pre-plan every element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character
rubrics_metrics.description:
- Know your characters intimately — what they want, fear, love, hate
- Plot grows out of character; characters drive action
- Listen to your characters — they will tell you what they want to do
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize deep, specific knowledge of characters' desires and fears as the engine of story; avoid forcing characters to obey a preconceived plot. Use character wants/conflicts to generate authentic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot emerges from character; not the other way around. The most authentic plots come from putting characters under pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate plot by creating obstacles and pressures that test characters' wants and weaknesses. Anti-pattern: outlining or contriving scenes that don't arise organically from character motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description:
- Dialogue should sound like real people speaking
- Read it aloud to test
- Each character must have a distinctive voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write dialogue that reflects natural speech rhythms and individual character, then read it aloud to check authenticity. Ensure each character's diction and patterns differ so voices are distinguishable on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting / Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the senses. Concrete sensory detail grounds the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor scenes with concrete, sensory specifics rather than abstract summary. Choose details that reveal character or mood; avoid overloading with irrelevant description.

rubrics_metrics.name: KFKD Radio (self-doubt and inner critics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The internal voices of self-doubt and self-aggrandizement; recognize and dismiss them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and name the contradictory internal voices that sabotage or inflate your work; consciously ignore or turn off those voices during drafting and revision so they don't block productivity or skew judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jealousy & Writer Envy
rubrics_metrics.description: Jealousy of other writers is a natural part of the writing life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge envy but do not let it drive your process; use it as information or motivation rather than a reason to compare and stall your own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverence for the Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat your subject and characters with respect; honesty matters more than cleverness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach material with seriousness and ethical attention; prefer truthful, emotionally honest choices over showy or glib cleverness that undermines authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broccoli (trust intuition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to your intuition — it knows what the story needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor gut instincts about scenes, lines, or choices even when they are small or odd; intuition can guide revision decisions and reveal what the work truly wants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index Cards & Notebooks (habitual observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry index cards and notebooks constantly to capture observations, snippets of dialogue, ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the habit of collecting small details and moments as they occur; use these raw fragments as fuel for scenes, descriptions, and authentic dialogue later in drafting and revision.
